title: Rules of Hooks Dynamic Validator
subtopicTitle: Hooks Linked List & Rules of Hooks
concept: Detecting Conditional or Shuffled Hook Calls
problemStatement: Implement `validateHookSequence(mountHooks, updateHooks)` that compares the sequence of hook types called on mount vs update. If update calls fewer hooks, more hooks, or a different hook type at any index, throws an Error detailing the exact violation.
interviewTrap: This is the exact runtime error React throws: 'Rendered fewer hooks than expected. This may be caused by an accidental early return statement.'

testCases.testFn: try { validateHookSequence(['useState', 'useEffect'], ['useEffect', 'useState']); return false; } catch (e) { return e.message.includes('Hook type mismatch'); }

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: The fundamental Rule of Hooks ('Only Call Hooks at the Top Level — do not call inside loops, conditions, or nested functions') exists because React relies exclusively on the sequential call order of hooks to match state. A dynamic validator detects hook count or type mismatches across renders and throws an error.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Maintain record of hooks called during initial mount: `expectedHookSequence = ['state', 'effect', 'state']`.
On subsequent re-renders, track each hook call index and type.
If a conditional statement omits a hook or changes the order (e.g. calling 'effect' when 'state' was expected):
Immediately detect mismatch: `Rendered fewer hooks than expected` or `Hook type mismatch at index i`.
Throw descriptive error matching React's internal invariant violation.
Validator confirms strict obedience to the Rules of Hooks.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React's `ReactFiberHooks.js`, if `updateWorkInProgressHook` finds that `nextHook` is null while the component is still executing hooks, React throws: `Error: Rendered more hooks than during the previous render`. If the component finishes with unvisited hooks left over, it throws: `Error: Rendered fewer hooks than during the previous render`.

complexity.time: O(H) validation over H hook calls.

verifiedRules: Hooks must be called in the exact same order on every render.
Violating call order corrupts internal linked list pointers and throws invariant errors.
